title: Dash AI Block
description: Schema for the [ai] section in dash.toml — structured, machine-readable metadata that enables AI agents and semantic search to reason about packages without executing or scraping. Validated on publish and indexed by the registry's semantic index.

summary.description: Human-readable, one-paragraph summary of the package's purpose and key characteristics. Unlike the [package].description field (which is a short tagline), the summary can be multiple sentences. Indexed for semantic search.
examples: HTTP client with automatic retries, typed responses, and a mock transport for tests. Supports pluggable transports and request/response interceptors.

intent.description: A term from the curated Dash capability taxonomy. Follows a hierarchical slash-separated naming convention. Enables exact-filter search: 'find me an X' becomes a filter, not a fuzzy search.

items.description: A functional capability identifier, typically dot-separated. Describes what the package does, not what it needs (which is in [capabilities]).

capabilities-declared.description: The functional capabilities the package offers (distinct from the security capabilities it requests in [capabilities]). These are indexed for capability-space search.

stability.description: Package lifecycle stage. 'experimental' = breaking changes possible; 'stable' = semver-guaranteed; 'maintenance' = critical fixes only; 'deprecated' = no active development. Maps to how MVS treats the package.

side-effects.description: Side-effect classification. 'none' = pure function (idempotent, no I/O); 'filesystem' = reads/writes local files; 'network' = makes network calls; 'global' = modifies global state. Agents use this to prefer pure libraries and reason about test isolation.

docs.description: Relative path to a machine-oriented documentation file (markdown with structured frontmatter). The registry indexes this for semantic search alongside the summary.

tool-interfaces.description: Relative path to a JSON file describing typed callable tool interfaces (JSON Schema / MCP-compatible tool definitions). Enables agent discovery of callable operations.

examples.description: Relative path to a directory containing runnable, version-verified examples. The registry executes each example against the actual package version and records pass/fail, so examples are known to work with the pinned version.

supersedes.description: A package reference (name@range) that this package supersedes. Provides an explicit migration edge so upgrade agents can plan a path off an abandoned library.

deprecated-in-favor-of.description: Package reference that this package is deprecated in favor of. The migration target for deprecation, for agents to plan a migration path.

items.description: Arbitrary classification tag for filtering and discovery.

tags.description: Arbitrary classification tags for the registry's search and filter indexes.

examples.summary: HTTP client with automatic retries, typed responses, and a mock transport for tests.
